title: Usage quotas & grace period comms scratch
content:
Goal: quick, empathetic internal comms draft we can iterate on. This is my personal scratchpad for CEO/Head of Product talking points + Q/A for support/GTM. Not for customers yet — internal only.

Context (short):
- We are introducing new usage quotas for free-tier orgs and a 72-hour grace period + soft throttling for overages on paid tiers.
- Reason: repeated short bursts causing noisy autoscaling and unpredictable latency spikes in shared-hosted pools. Also need to limit abuse and reduce emergency capacity spend.
- Timing: staged rollout starting 2026-03-15 (internal pilot), org-wide opt-in to grace window on 2026-04-06, enforcement (hard caps) 2026-05-01.

What leadership should say (top-line):
- Opening line: "We owe our customers predictable performance. To keep latency consistent while avoiding surprise bills and unnecessary extra capacity, we’re introducing modest usage quotas + a temporary grace window for overage."
- Reassure: "This is about stability and fairness—most active teams won't notice any change; high-burst workloads will get clearer signals and options."
- Highlight options: "We’ll offer easy upgrade paths (burst add-on, reserved capacity for Dedicated, or private deployment consults) and one-click overrides for critical jobs."
- Tone: matter-of-fact, solutions-focused, not punitive. Emphasize listening and fast follow-up.

Key bullets for all-hands slide (short):
- Why: reduce noisy extremes, protect latency SLOs for everyone.
- What: quotas by tier + 72-hour soft grace that lets spiky traffic through but throttles after sustained overage.
- When: pilot 3/15, opt-in 4/6, enforcement 5/1.
- What’s in it for customers: more predictable latency, fewer surprise scaling incidents, clearer upgrade guidance.
- Who to talk to: CS escalation channel (#cs-quotas), Solutions Eng for dedicated capacity, Billing for metering questions.

Anticipated internal Qs (and short answers)
- Q: Will this cause customer downtime?
  A: No — grace period and soft throttling prevents immediate cutoffs. Hard caps only after repeated sustained overage and customer is notified.
- Q: How big are the quotas?
  A: Tiered. Free: conservative (X tokens/day), Starter: Y tokens/day, Standard/Pro: larger. Exact numbers coming from Pricing & Eng (see linked confluence).
- Q: How will this affect embeddings/long-loop batch jobs?
  A: We’re exempting scheduled batch jobs that register via job API (team to build registration endpoint). For ad-hoc long-running streams, we’ll provide guidance and a best-practice checklist.
- Q: Are there refunds for accidental overages?
  A: Short answer: case-by-case during pilot. We expect to offer credits in clear edge cases. Policy TBD (billing team).
- Q: How do we detect abuse vs legitimate burst?
  A: Heuristics: rapid token burn with many unique prompts + identical IP patterns; combined with rate-of-change signals. Manual review for borderline cases.

Support playbook (draft, short):
- 0-72 hours after first overage: customer receives in-product banner + email explaining grace window and links to docs.
- 72-96 hours sustained overage: soft throttles applied (queueing, slower response). Auto-ticket created in Zendesk, flagged to CS team.
- >96 hours or repeat within 30 days: hard cap applied; CS assigned; Solutions Eng outreach for dedicated options.
- Escalation: if customer is running critical safety or compliance workloads, contact SRE + Head of Solutions Eng for immediate override.

Internal TODOs (open items I need help with):
- [ ] Pricing to confirm quota numbers and visible thresholds (assign: Ravi)
- [ ] UX: in-product banner copy and CTA + link to request fast override (assign: Marta)
- [ ] Eng: registration endpoint for batch jobs + telemetry for heuristics (assign: Noah)
- [ ] Legal/Billing: grace credits policy and terms update (ask: legal counsel)

Draft in-product banner copy (super rough):
"Heads up: we’ve enabled usage quotas to protect performance. You’re currently within the 72‑hour grace window for recent overage. Learn more or request temporary increase."

Script snippets for CS (tone & sample messages):
- Empathetic, proactive: "Thanks for flagging this — we’ve put you in a 72-hour grace window so your jobs continue to run while we review. If you anticipate sustained traffic, we can walk through options (burst credits, reserved capacity)."
- If customer angry: "I hear you — we’re sorry for the surprise. We rolled the grace window in to avoid immediate cuts. We’ll review and advise next steps; if this was unintended, we can consider a one-time credit during the pilot."

Metrics to show at product review (suggested):
- % of orgs hitting quota vs tier (daily/weekly)
- Latency P50/P95 before vs after pilot window per pool
- Number of manual overrides granted and time-to-respond
- Cost saved from reduced emergency scaling (estimate)

Risks / open concerns:
- Miscommunication -> customer backlash. Mitigation: extra CS training + proactive emails to high-usage orgs before opt-in.
- Edge cases (scheduled batch) need tech work quickly. If missed, we risk breaking legitimate jobs. Prioritize registration endpoint.
- Measurement lag (billing pipes) could cause false positives. Need a short-term manual review step in pilot.

Backchannel notes to myself:
- Keep CEO script < 90s. Focus on "why" + "what we’re doing to help".
- Do not leak numbers publicly until pricing approves.
- We should prepare a short sample customer advisory for top 20 high-usage accounts. Draft draft list: AcornAI, NovaForms, Shoplytics (ask AMs to confirm).

Questions I still have (for meeting 3/2):
- Exact quota thresholds per tier? (Ravi)
- Can Eng get the batch-registration MVP by 3/12? (Noah)
- Who signs the final customer advisory? Legal or Product? (Marta)

Notes for 3/2 sync:
- Quick run through of pilot timeline + responsibilities.
- Share sample Zendesk templates.
- Confirm channels: #cs-quotas, #eng-quotas, #pilot-ops.

Rough escalation contacts (short):
- CS lead: Marta Ruiz
- Product lead: Aisha Patel
- Eng SRE on-call: Pager (SRE rotation)
- Solutions Eng escalation: Noah Freeman

End of scratch — will iterate after 3/2.
